To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ATE-APT complex can target PSMA-overexpressed prostate cancer cells in vivo and in vitro and can be used to effectively deliver miRNAs to PCa bone tumors.
the APT-conjugated atelectocolagen delivery system is a promising strategy for the targeted therapy of bone metastasis in PCa.
the PSMA-targeted delivery of miRNA/atecollagen complex is more effective than that of miRNA/ atecollagen complex in suppressing bone metastasis of prostate cancer in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of ATE/ATP as a new drug delivery system for the treatment of prostate cancer bone metastasis.
the design of ATE-based miRNA delivery systems for the treatment of bone metastatic PCa.
the development of a novel PSMA-targeted miRNA delivery system to treat PCa bone metastases, which may be a promising approach to improve the efficacy and reduce side effects in the treatment of PCa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the APT-ATE–miR complex can be used as a targeted delivery system to deliver miRNA to PSMA+ PCa bone metastases.
ATE–APT-mediated miRNA delivery can be used as a promising strategy for the treatment of PCa bone metastases.
ATE–APT can effectively target PSMA-positive PCa cells, which is an effective strategy for treating bone metastasis in PCa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATE-APT complex is a novel, effective and promising delivery system for miRNA to treat bone-metastasis prostate cancer in vivo.
ATE–APT can be used to deliver miRNA to PCa bone tumors and may be used as a potential therapeutic strategy for PCa bone metastatic tumors.
the miRNA/ATE-APT complex can be used as a novel targeted gene delivery system for the treatment of PCa bone metastases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
APT conjugation to ATE increases the transfection efficiency and anticancer effect of miRNA/ ATE complexes.
the ATE–APT complex is a promising tool for targeted delivery and transgene expression in PCa bone metastases.

APT-conjugated atecollagen can be used as a targeted delivery system to deliver miRNA to PCa bone-metastasis cells, thereby inhibiting PCa bone metastatic tumor growth and increasing the survival time of mice with bone-metastasized PCa.
